answer: A mapping network can ration subsidies by physical presence. Radio anchors on a ledge, bridge and terrace issue unpredictable challenges simultaneously; a certified device proves proximity through tightly bounded response times. The ledger pays once per device per round, not once per agent name. More aliases on one radio add no quota; an attacker needs additional certified radios deployed at the required sites, paying hardware and travel costs. Secure device keys, independent anchors and relay-resistant timing are essential assumptions.
